newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open flat to weaker.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open flat to weaker.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open flat to weaker Monday as gold was fixed in London at its lowest since Feb 12.
Dealers in Europe said the weak fixing could encourage prices to hit lower levels.
COMEX August gold was called $0.50 to $1.00 lower from Friday's close of $339.40 an ounce. London bullion was fixed at $336.95 this morning. Bullion here was quoted by dealers at $336.70/$337.20.
COMEX July silver was called flat to down 2.00 cents from Friday's close at $4.712.
The weakening in gold was due to a seasonal slowdown in demand in the northern hemisphere and a strong dollar, dealers said overnight.
COMEX gold stocks Friday rose 12,278 ounces to 841,145 ounces, but silver stocks fell 1,652,432 ounces to 186,131,387 ounces.
NYMEX July platinum was called flat to off $0.50 from the previous close of $415.20, with NYMEX September palladium called unchanged from Friday's finish of $172.85.
The market was still awaiting confirmation of when shipments of the long-delayed Russian platinum group metal exports actually start.
